decision.unit: one VM-isolate per tenant incarnation; many tenant isolates share one OS process, as GraalVM isolates do
decision.processSandboxRole: optional defense in depth; never a precondition for admitting an untrusted tenant, and never claimed unless implemented and tested

design.unit: a tenant incarnation owns one VM-isolate: its own heap, actors, generation and failure domain; multiple actors may live within it
design.memory: each isolate has a private heap with an enforced per-tenant cap; tenant-owned mutable state never crosses into another tenant; cross-tenant delivery copies or re-encodes values
design.actor_execution: no actor reentrancy, including across suspension or independent lock queues
design.resource_accounting: limit tenants per process, actors, heap and inflight work per tenant; account host overhead separately; the scalar reference turn is non-reentrant even if tenant inflight capacity exceeds one
design.termination: the host can end one tenant's running guest code without the guest's cooperation, or through checks the trusted code producer inserted, and without ending the process or any other tenant
design.failure: a guest trap, out-of-bounds access, stack overflow, heap-limit or deadline breach ends only that isolate; the process and every other tenant continue; restart gets fresh handles and memory
design.fairness: scheduling is fair per tenant, not per actor; a tenant with many ready actors cannot starve a quiet tenant
design.capabilities: fail-closed denial of FFI, WASI, filesystem, network, native memory and host imports unless explicitly authorized; guest code calls only the host API, never libc
design.trust: logical heap/arena quotas or a shared language context are not an isolate; an isolate needs a private heap, enforced limits and independent termination
design.untrusted: untrusted tenants run only in a VM-isolate whose guest code came from a trusted producer: a validated Wasm module (lowered or engine-compiled) or Truffle inside a Graal isolate; tenants never supply native code or raw CIL
design.aot: signed/approved native artifacts required before any unsafe deserialization; caller-supplied SHA is only identity check
design.shutdown: fence queued/running work, drain references and resource loans, then reclaim; a killed isolate's guest turns are abandoned but host-owned loans still drain before stop
design.root_authority: Opaque authority belongs to one root VM; matching tenant ID and numeric generation from another root never grants access
design.tenant_id_validation: ASCII [A-Za-z0-9_.-], 1..128 bytes, excluding reserved path components '.' and '..'; strings are identifiers, not filesystem paths
design.cpu_accounting: turn deadlines and scheduling fairness count each tenant's own CPU time, not wall-clock time or turn counts, so a neighbor crowding the CPU cannot get an innocent tenant killed or starved
design.mail_quotas: queued mail is bounded per tenant and per host in bytes, not only per mailbox; delivery and actor retirement refund it; a dead isolate returns all of it
design.host_calls: every guest-controlled argument to a host call is validated before use, so no guest input can fault the host process; no guest-reachable path takes a process-wide lock
design.queued_work: callers queued behind a running turn are rejected promptly once the tenant stops admitting work; they never wait for a possibly spinning turn to return
design.instrumentation: runtime instrumentation (probes and JIT-recompiled tracing variants) follows attolang.governed-instrumentation.v1: operator-only, tenant-scoped, produced by the trusted code producer

securityBoundary.enforcedBy: the per-tenant isolate plus the trusted code producer (Wasm validator and lowerer, or the Graal compiler), exactly as Graal's compiler is the boundary for its isolates

refusedUntrustedGuestCode.native: tenant-supplied native code can address anything in the process
refusedUntrustedGuestCode.cil: CoreCLR has no in-process isolate: one process-wide GC heap, no runtime IL verification, no AppDomains, and an AssemblyLoadContext is not a security boundary

acceptedSharedProcessRisks: a bug in the runtime, the Wasm validator, the lowerer or the Graal compiler can reach every tenant in the process
a crash outside guest code ends every tenant in the process
speculative and timing side channels between tenants are not addressed by this contract

java.isolate: one Graal polyglot isolate (own Engine and heap) per tenant
java.termination: Truffle safepoint cancellation of the tenant context
java.caveat: polyglot isolates and SandboxPolicy.UNTRUSTED require Oracle GraalVM, not Community Edition

llvm.isolate: TenantVm cage: private 4 GiB window plus guard per tenant, addressed as cage + u32 offset
llvm.termination: interrupt the tenant's carrier threads; no compiler-inserted checks needed
llvm.caveat: the runtime does not enforce the addressing rule; validated Wasm lowered by wasm2c is the enforced path

wasm.isolate: one Wasmtime Store + Instance per tenant
wasm.termination: per-Store kill flag checked from an epoch callback, or fuel
wasm.caveat: epochs are per Engine, so targeted kill needs a per-Store flag; one Store runs on one thread at a time

net.isolate: TenantVm cage on the shared native core, called from .NET through TenantVmCApi
net.termination: native carrier interrupt (native threads, not CLR threads)
net.memoryCap: cage commit limit; tenants add no CLR GC load
net.caveat: direct CIL stays a first-class backend for trusted tenants only

forge.caveat: untrusted tenants are refused until Forge emits validated Wasm or an equivalent proven boundary

cranelift.caveat: direct native JIT output is not validated; untrusted tenants are refused until it routes through validated Wasm

js.isolate: candidate: one V8 isolate (Worker with resourceLimits) per tenant, exposing no Node built-ins to guest code
js.caveat: a Worker that can reach Node built-ins is not an isolate under this contract
